questions.question: When does an incident's duration require public communication?

expected.mustContain: All incidents with a total duration of more than 5 minutes should be publicly communicated as quickly as possible

questions.notes: Tests retrieval of a duration threshold rather than a generic incident keyword.

questions.question: What remediation SLA applies to a vulnerability with a CVSSv3 score of 8.2?

expected.mustContain: 7.0-8.9 (High) | `~severity::2` | `~priority::2` | N/A | 30 day SLA

questions.notes: Requires mapping a numeric score to the correct severity band and SLA.

questions.question: At what expense amount must a US team member submit a receipt?

expected.mustContain: US Team Members are required to only submit receipts for any expenses over $50 USD.

questions.notes: Tests a regional exception and a monetary threshold.

questions.question: When does a sick absence become a leave of absence?

expected.mustContain: Sick absences that are 6 days or longer are considered a **leave of absence**.

questions.notes: Tests retrieval of the six-day condition in the time-off policy.

questions.question: How is a change categorized if it will cause downtime in Production?

expected.mustContain: If a change is going to cause downtime to the Production environment, it is always categorized a `C1`.

questions.notes: Requires applying the downtime condition to the criticality rule.

questions.question: How should a system containing several data types be classified?

expected.mustContain: the system should be classified at the highest data classification level of the data being stored

questions.notes: Checks retrieval of the rule for combined data types.

questions.question: When does planned PTO require special permission?

expected.mustContain: for time off exceeding 25 consecutive calendar days (including weekends and holidays), special permission is required

questions.notes: Tests a threshold whose count includes weekends and holidays.

questions.question: Can an expense more than 90 days old still be reimbursed, and under what condition?

expected.mustContain: Expense claims over 90 days from purchase date will not be reimbursed unless approved by the Manager.

questions.notes: Requires retrieving both the rule and its manager-approval exception.

questions.question: Who can declare an incident resolved?

expected.mustContain: only the owner of the incident can declare an incident resolved

questions.notes: Tests a precise incident ownership responsibility.

questions.question: What is the normal completion deadline for offboarding deprovisioning tasks?

expected.mustContain: all tasks expected to be completed within 5 working days

questions.notes: Checks the operational deadline in the offboarding standard.

questions.question: For a High non-FedRAMP dependency vulnerability, what is the baseline remediation SLA and what relief is appropriate when the vendor delays the fix?

expected.mustContain: 7.0-8.9 (High) | `~severity::2` | `~priority::2` | N/A | 30 day SLA
An exception to extend the SLA is appropriate in this case.

questions.notes: Combines the baseline severity SLA with the separate exception procedure for delayed vendor fixes.

questions.question: What approvals are needed for a $2,000 conference registration and its business-critical travel?

expected.mustContain: Manager + VP approval: $1,000.01 - $10,000
Team Members must receive Manager approval for any proposed business critical trips.

questions.notes: Requires the G&D cost tier and the separate travel-policy approval rule.

questions.question: When are offboarding cases created, and how long do departments normally have to finish their tasks?

expected.mustContain: the Offboarding Parent and Child Cases will be created in HelpLab.
all tasks expected to be completed within 5 working days

questions.notes: Joins the workflow trigger on the general page to the deadline in the standards page.

questions.question: Which two special rules apply when planning scheduled maintenance classified as C1?

expected.mustContain: planned infrastructure changes - require a minimum 2-week lead time
Scheduled maintenance that is a `C1` should be treated as an undeclared incident.

questions.notes: Combines the change-planning lead time with the incident-management treatment.

questions.question: How should an access token be classified, and what storage precaution applies when using it from a command line?

expected.mustContain: derive their classification from the highest classification of the data they protect.
Avoid storing secrets in unencrypted files or using them directly on the CLI.

questions.notes: Requires both the data-classification rule and the separate operational storage guidance.

questions.question: What can the term SLA refer to in this handbook?

expected.mustContain: Availability SLA commitments to the customer
track the time from detection to remediation and fix availability for vulnerability findings

questions.notes: Captures SLA as a customer availability commitment and as an internal vulnerability-remediation timeframe.

questions.question: What responsibilities can an owner have in incident management and data classification?

expected.mustContain: only the owner of the incident can declare an incident resolved
Data Owners shall determine the classification of data in accordance with this standard.

questions.notes: Distinguishes ownership of an incident from ownership of a data type.

questions.question: What are the two meanings of Critical in the incident and vulnerability severity schemes?

expected.mustContain: Severity:1 **Critical** | **Customer Impact:**
9.0-10.0 (Critical) | `~severity::1` | `~priority::1`

questions.notes: Separates an operational incident impact level from a CVSS vulnerability score band.
